name: Main Gate (Gwanghwamun)
proactivePrompt: Welcome to Gyeongbokgung Palace. The ticket booth is 100 meters ahead. Tickets are 3,000 won and entry is free if you're wearing a hanbok.
knowledgeSummary: Gwanghwamun is the main and largest gate of Gyeongbokgung Palace. It originally had a watchtower structure.

surroundings.back: Heungnyemun Gate and the palace grounds

name: Ticket Booth
proactivePrompt: The ticket booth is just ahead on your right. They accept credit cards and cash. Lines are typically shorter on weekday mornings.
knowledgeSummary: Ticket booth for entering Gyeongbokgung Palace. Regular adult ticket is 3,000 KRW. Closed on Tuesdays.

name: Geunjeongjeon Throne Hall
proactivePrompt: You're approaching the main throne hall, Geunjeongjeon. Feel free to ask me anything about the architecture or history.
knowledgeSummary: Geunjeongjeon is the main throne hall where the king held official ceremonies. Built in 1395. The name means 'industrious governance'.

surroundings.front: Geunjeongmun Gate and the large paved courtyard

facilities.waterFountains: Near the restrooms to the east

name: Gyeonghoeru Pavilion
proactivePrompt: This is Gyeonghoeru Pavilion, used for royal banquets. Visitors cannot enter, but it's a popular photo spot.
knowledgeSummary: Gyeonghoeru Pavilion is a large elevated pavilion resting on 48 stone pillars, overlooking an artificial pond. Used for state banquets and receiving foreign envoys.

surroundings.back: Sujeongjeon Hall and the palace walls

name: National Palace Museum
proactivePrompt: The National Palace Museum is on your left. Admission is separate (5,000 won). Would you like me to show you the entrance on the map?
knowledgeSummary: The National Palace Museum of Korea houses a massive collection of art and objects from the Joseon Dynasty.

name: Heungnyemun Gate
proactivePrompt: You are at Heungnyemun, the second inner gate. Have your tickets ready for inspection here.
knowledgeSummary: Heungnyemun is the second gate of Gyeongbokgung. It was originally built in 1426, destroyed during the Japanese invasion, and reconstructed.

surroundings.back: Gwanghwamun Gate and the outer courtyard

name: Sajeongjeon Hall
proactivePrompt: This is Sajeongjeon, where the King conducted daily state affairs. Notice the sundial out front.
knowledgeSummary: Sajeongjeon was the executive office where the King met with officials daily. 'Sajeong' means 'deeply pondering before deciding'.

name: Gangnyeongjeon Hall
proactivePrompt: You've reached Gangnyeongjeon, the King's living quarters. The roof has no white ridge, a unique feature of royal sleeping quarters.
knowledgeSummary: Gangnyeongjeon served as the King's primary living and sleeping quarters. The lack of a top roof ridge signifies the King's status as the metaphorical dragon.

name: Gyotaejeon Hall
proactivePrompt: This is Gyotaejeon, the Queen's residence. Be sure to check out the beautiful terraced garden directly behind it.
knowledgeSummary: Gyotaejeon was the primary living quarters for the Queen. It was the center of the inner court.

name: Amisan Garden
proactivePrompt: You are looking at Amisan, the Queen's private terraced garden. Notice the intricately carved hexagonal chimneys.
knowledgeSummary: Amisan is an artificial mound with a terraced garden built for the Queen. The beautifully decorated brick chimneys are National Treasures.

name: Hyangwonjeong Pavilion
proactivePrompt: This beautiful hexagonal pavilion on the island is Hyangwonjeong. It's one of the most picturesque spots in the palace.
knowledgeSummary: Hyangwonjeong is a two-story hexagonal pavilion built on an artificial island. It was constructed in 1873 for King Gojong's leisure.

surroundings.back: The main palace complexes to the south

name: National Folk Museum of Korea
proactivePrompt: The tall pagoda-style building is the National Folk Museum. Entry is free if you want to learn about traditional Korean life.
knowledgeSummary: The National Folk Museum of Korea illustrates the history of traditional life of the Korean people. The building design combines various famous historical structures.

facilities.cafe: Museum cafe on the first floor

name: Sinmumun (North Gate)
proactivePrompt: This is Sinmumun, the north gate. If you exit here, you'll see the Blue House (Cheongwadae) right across the street.
knowledgeSummary: Sinmumun is the northern gate of Gyeongbokgung. Exiting this gate leads directly to the former presidential residence, the Blue House.

facilities.restrooms: Just outside the gate near the Blue House

name: Yeongchumun (West Gate)
proactivePrompt: You are at Yeongchumun, the west gate. This leads out to the Seochon neighborhood, famous for cafes and galleries.
knowledgeSummary: Yeongchumun, the Autumn Gate, is the western entrance to the palace. It was primarily used by civil and military officials.

name: Geonchunmun (East Gate)
proactivePrompt: This is Geonchunmun, the east gate. Exiting here takes you towards the Bukchon Hanok Village and Samcheong-dong.
knowledgeSummary: Geonchunmun, the Spring Gate, is the eastern entrance. It was historically used by the royal family and their relatives.

name: King Sejong Statue
proactivePrompt: You are at the statue of King Sejong the Great, the inventor of the Korean alphabet, Hangul.
knowledgeSummary: A massive golden statue of King Sejong the Great, the 4th king of Joseon, located in the center of Gwanghwamun Square. Underneath is a museum dedicated to his achievements.

surroundings.left: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts

facilities.restrooms: Inside the underground museum (entrance behind the statue)

name: Admiral Yi Sun-sin Statue
proactivePrompt: This is the statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin, Korea's greatest naval hero. Notice the turtle ship miniature at the base.
knowledgeSummary: A towering statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin, who saved Korea during the Imjin War in the 16th century using his famous Turtle Ships.

name: Cheonggyecheon Stream Plaza
proactivePrompt: You are at Cheonggyecheon Plaza, the start of the 11km urban stream. It's a great place to sit and relax.
knowledgeSummary: Cheonggyecheon is a restored public recreation space in downtown Seoul. The plaza features a famous spiral sculpture called 'Spring'.

facilities.restrooms: Public restrooms down by the stream path

name: Gwanghwamun Station (Exit 9)
proactivePrompt: You are near Gwanghwamun Station Exit 9, directly in the square. Watch out for crowds here.
knowledgeSummary: Exit 9 of Gwanghwamun Station connects directly to Haechi Madang, the underground plaza beneath Gwanghwamun Square.

name: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts
proactivePrompt: The large building with the grand staircase is the Sejong Center, Seoul's largest arts and cultural complex.
knowledgeSummary: The Sejong Center is the largest arts and cultural complex in Seoul, featuring a massive pipe organ and various theaters.

facilities.cafe: Multiple cafes inside and around the stairs
